responsibility: Stage three. Apply the simplicity threshold, cluster tag co-occurrence into archetypes, measure per-archetype demand, competition density and release-date trends, and assemble the opportunity matrix. Writes aggregate outputs into analysis_results.

external: scikit-learn or scipy (clustering; see open questions)

design_notes: Pure transformation over games_enriched and game_tags. Re-runnable for an existing run_id after a threshold change, with no refetch.
An archetype is a tag/genre cluster, not a single tag. Single-tag views are still produced for the tag summary table, but the opportunity matrix is cluster-level.
Competition density is measured over past releases and describes the market those games entered, not today's market. This framing must survive into the output labels.
All results are descriptive. No causal or predictive claim is attached to a trend slope, and every aggregate carries its sample size.

public_interface.name: apply_simplicity_filter
public_interface.signature: def apply_simplicity_filter(frame: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, int]]
public_interface.description: Splits the enriched frame into the 'buildable' subset and a rejection tally. Rows with NULL complexity_score are excluded from the subset but remain available for density counting.

public_interface.name: cluster_tags
public_interface.signature: def cluster_tags(tags: pd.DataFrame, frame: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> TagClusterResult
public_interface.description: Builds a tag co-occurrence matrix over the candidate set and clusters it into archetypes. Each cluster gets a deterministic id and a human-readable label built from its highest-weight member tags.

public_interface.name: compute_tag_trends
public_interface.signature: def compute_tag_trends(frame: pd.DataFrame, assignments: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Per archetype, median estimated sales and release count per sub-window across the trailing window, plus a slope. Every row carries n per sub-window.

public_interface.name: compute_competition_density
public_interface.signature: def compute_competition_density(frame: pd.DataFrame, assignments: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Release count per archetype inside the trailing window, adjusted for overall catalog growth so a rising tide is not read as rising competition.

public_interface.name: compute_demand
public_interface.signature: def compute_demand(frame: pd.DataFrame, assignments: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Per archetype, median estimated sales and median review count over the trailing window, with the interquartile range retained so a single outlier hit is visible rather than hidden in a median.

public_interface.name: build_opportunity_matrix
public_interface.signature: def build_opportunity_matrix(demand: pd.DataFrame, competition: pd.DataFrame, simplicity: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Implements FORMULATION.md section 6. Columns: cluster_id, label, n_games, demand_z, competition_z, simplicity_z, opportunity_score, median_estimated_sales_mid, median_complexity, releases_in_window.

public_interface.name: build_tag_summary
public_interface.signature: def build_tag_summary(frame: pd.DataFrame, tags: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Single-tag view: per tag, game count, median complexity, median estimated sales, median positive review percentage, median price.

public_interface.name: run_analysis
public_interface.signature: def run_analysis(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, params: AnalysisParams, *, parameters_version: str, on_event: EventSink) -> AnalysisReport
public_interface.description: Stage entry point. Reads games_enriched and game_tags, writes analysis_results rows of type opportunity_matrix, tag_summary, tag_clusters, tag_trends and competition_density.

invariants: Every aggregate row carries its sample size (n_games); no median is published without it
Clusters smaller than min_cluster_size are excluded from opportunity scoring and reported separately, never dropped silently
Clustering is deterministic for a fixed input and seed; cluster ids are stable within a run
z-scores are computed over the scored cluster population of the same run and are therefore comparable within a run but not across runs
All parameters come from AnalysisParams; no threshold literal appears in code
edge_cases: Empty or tiny candidate set (fewer rows than min_cluster_size) -> stage succeeds, writes empty results with an explanatory warning event; the UI must render 'not enough data' rather than an empty chart
Zero-variance feature when computing z-scores -> z defined as 0 for all clusters rather than a division by zero
A single archetype dominating the candidate set -> reported, since a near-degenerate clustering invalidates comparison
Games with an unparseable release_date -> excluded from trend and density windows, included in overall medians, and counted
Tags below min_tag_votes -> excluded before clustering
Games carrying no tags at all -> excluded from clustering, retained in the tag-independent summaries
Trailing window containing fewer than two sub-windows -> no slope computed, field left NULL rather than estimated from one point
Ties in opportunity_score -> deterministic ordering by cluster_id

unit: apply_simplicity_filter honours the threshold at the boundary and tallies each rejection reason
cluster_tags is deterministic across repeated calls on the same input
cluster_tags on a synthetic set with two obviously separated tag groups recovers exactly those two clusters
compute_competition_density normalizes for catalog growth as specified on a synthetic two-year catalog
compute_demand retains the interquartile range and the outlier is visible in it
build_opportunity_matrix reproduces hand-computed z-scores and the weighted combination
zero-variance inputs produce z=0 rather than NaN or a raised exception
clusters below min_cluster_size are excluded from scoring and appear in clusters_below_min_size
an empty enriched frame produces an empty but well-formed result set
integration: run_analysis over a fixture database writes all five analysis_types with the expected schemas

non_goals: No presentation formatting, no chart objects, no case-study prose (that is reporting)
No predictive modelling or forecasting of future demand
open_questions: Clustering method: co-occurrence + hierarchical/agglomerative clustering is the straw man. Alternatives are community detection on a tag graph or simple frequent-itemset mining. Needs a decision before implementation, and the choice must be recorded in FORMULATION.md section 6.
Whether an archetype should be anchored to the primary genre plus its top-k tags rather than derived purely from tag co-occurrence.
Catalog-growth adjustment for competition density: normalize by total releases in the same window, or by a fitted growth curve.
